close_reason: Added '# Optional methods and supports_type' section explaining the unconditional registration contract. Consumers building a session-capability response must separately consult supports_type. Bundled with the count-fix from JMAP-ic0j.7 since both edits target the same rustdoc.
description:
crate-jmap-calendars-server/src/backend.rs:170-182 documents that the calendars handler library deliberately does NOT consult `supports_type` (unlike mail-server which short-circuits `handle_search_snippet_get` via `supports_type::<SearchSnippet>()`).

That divergence is documented on the trait method. But the consequences for the consumer at the registration API at src/lib.rs:97-190 (`register_calendars_handlers`) are NOT documented.

What's actually unspecified at the lib.rs API surface:

1. A backend whose `supports_type::<CalendarEventNotification>()` returns `false` still has all FIVE `CalendarEventNotification/*` methods registered with the dispatcher. The handler will be invoked.

2. The handler does not check `supports_type` (per the trait note) and forwards to the backend.

3. The backend's `get_objects::<CalendarEventNotification>()` will be invoked; the backend impl decides what to return. Returning `Ok((vec![], vec![ids...]))` (empty + every requested id in not_found) is the typical "not implemented" answer.

4. Clients cannot tell "this server supports notifications but the account has none" from "this server does not implement notifications" — both look like an empty response.

The lib.rs `register_calendars_handlers` rustdoc says nothing about this. It just lists all 19 methods (correct count per JMAP-ic0j.7) as if they were uniformly supported. A consumer who reads ONLY the registration function rustdoc and not the trait method rustdoc deeper in `backend.rs` will not learn that the consumer's session-capability builder is the ONLY place that respects the type's optionality.

What callers cannot rely on:
- That `register_calendars_handlers` honours the backend's `supports_type` answers. (It does not; backend.rs:170-182 explicitly says so, but the registration API does not surface that.)
- That the consumer's session-capability output and the dispatcher's method coverage will agree without the consumer separately consulting `supports_type` in their session builder.

Fix: add a `# Optional methods` section to the lib.rs:78-96 rustdoc summarising the trait-method note: "every method below is registered unconditionally; consumers building a session-capability response must consult `supports_type::<T>()` separately to decide which capability URIs to advertise. The dispatcher will invoke handlers even when the backend reports the type unsupported."

This is the API-contract supplement of JMAP-ic0j.25 (which addressed the rustdoc on the trait method). The trait method rustdoc is correct after .25; the registration function rustdoc remains silent.
title: register_calendars_handlers consequences of supports_type non-use undocumented at the registration API
